grades.quote: Unlike physical memory protection values described in Section 3.7, PMAs do not vary by execution context.
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary context distinguishing PMAs from PMP, but no PMP entry-matching or permission rules.

grades.quote: An optional physical memory protection (PMP) unit provides per-hart machine-mode control registers to allow physical memory access privileges (read, write, execute) to be specified for each physical memory region. The PMP values are checked in parallel with the PMA checks described in Section 3.6.
grades.reason: Explains region permissions and which privilege modes undergo checks, but omits entry priority and whole-access matching rules.
Describes supported access-type PMAs, not how PMP entries authorize accesses.

grades.quote: PMP entries are statically prioritized. The lowest-numbered PMP entry that matches any byte of an access determines whether that access succeeds or fails. The matching PMP entry must match all bytes of an access, or the access fails, irrespective of the L, R, W, and X bits.
grades.reason: Directly explains PMP entry priority, whole-access matching, permission and lock bits, privilege handling, and defaults when no entry matches.
